places.name: Bentsen-Rio Grande Valley State Park
places.coord_point: point printed on the official park page (type not labelled)
places.blurb: Rio Grande Valley park in Mission, next to the National Butterfly Center, with tent-only walk-in sites a 3/4-mile walk from the lot.
places.status_note: Cafe closed per the official page. Official page shows an active alert (text not readable in my fetch; the link suggests a screwworm notice, unconfirmed). Cars are not allowed inside the park.
places.notes: CANDIDATE NAMES, ten chosen by me for this batch: Armillary (chosen, written to _author), Ephemeris, Almucantar, Zenith, Nadir, Meridian, Hesper, Plumbline, Vernal, Terminator. COORDINATES: the TPWD page prints Latitude 26.186987 and Longitude -98.381888; both confirmed in the raw HTML. Wikipedia infobox gives 26.17306, -98.38250, about 1.5 km away (under 2 km, so noted only); official used. ACREAGE 764 and county Hidalgo come from Wikipedia (the TPWD page prints neither). CAMPING: the /stay path returned 404; camping was read from /fees-facilities/campsites: 5 primitive walk-in tent-only sites, up to 8 people, $15 per night, 3/4 mile from the parking lot, reserved online. The page also says a 60-person group hall can be booked; I did not read that on its own page. Hours 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. Customer service (512) 389-8900. Reservation link is the one printed on the campsites page. DARKSKY: the darksky.org places page would not render in my fetch (403 on WebFetch; its static HTML has no Texas list). A web search of darksky.org surfaced Texas designations (Copper Breaks, Enchanted Rock, South Llano River, Big Bend Ranch, Caprock Canyons, Devils River Dark Sky Sanctuary, Black Gap WMA); none of the nine places appeared in it. The Texas list is therefore not confirmed complete.

places.name: Colorado Bend State Park

places.status_note: Entrance road can flood during heavy rains (official page). Official page says to call for closure updates. Active alerts are shown on the page; their text was not readable in my fetch.
places.notes: COORDINATES: TPWD prints Latitude 31.022965 and Longitude -98.442401, both confirmed in the raw HTML. Wikipedia infobox gives 31.05389, -98.49222, about 5.9 km away (over 2 km); official used. COUNTY: Wikipedia says mostly San Saba County, with a smaller part in Lampasas County where the public has no access; recorded San Saba. ACREAGE 5,328.3 from Wikipedia (TPWD prints an elevation of 1,025 feet, no acreage). NEAREST TOWN: TPWD address is Bend, TX 76824; Wikipedia names San Saba as nearest city. CAMPING, from /fees-facilities/campsites: drive-up primitive sites ($15, 8 people, 15 sites, self-contained RVs up to 20 ft allowed, no hookups of any kind); walk-in tent-only primitive sites ($13, 8 people, page numbers them #1-29); hike-in backcountry sites in the river and windmill areas ($10, 4 people, no water or toilets, containerized stoves only); group camps Grey Fox and Canyon ($35, max 16) and River Area ($75, max 48). The page says the park often reaches capacity and recommends reservations. Customer service (512) 389-8900. The /stay path returned 404. DARKSKY: none found (see Bentsen notes for the search). LP: no official published reading seen on the pages I read; not exhaustively searched.

places.name: Amistad National Recreation Area
places.coord_point: Wikipedia infobox point for the park; the NPS page prints no coordinates and the visitor centre or headquarters is not located on it
nearby: Ciudad Acuña, Coahuila (across Amistad Dam, per Wikipedia)
places.blurb: Huge Amistad reservoir west of Del Rio: first-come campgrounds, reservable group sites, and lake-shore backcountry camping.
places.notes: COORDINATES: the NPS planyourvisit page prints none. The point is the Wikipedia infobox point 29.43667, -101.05000. It is not the visitor centre (not named on the NPS page) or headquarters. COUNTY Val Verde, ACREAGE 58,500 and nearest city Del Rio from Wikipedia. NPS mailing address 10477 Highway 90 West, Del Rio, TX 78840, phone (830) 775-7491 (page footer; the page does not say whether it is the visitor centre). CAMPING from the NPS camping page: five first-come, no-reservation campgrounds (Governors Landing, Rough Canyon, San Pedro, Spur 406, 277 North), $6 to $10 per site. Only Governors Landing has running water to shared spigots and takes RVs up to 28 ft. RVs have no hookups; an RV dump station is on the road to the Diablo East boat ramp. Group sites (Rock Quarry, San Pedro, 277 North) need a reservation on recreation.gov, $35 to $155 by group-size tier. Backcountry camping is permitted on the lake waters and shoreline, not within a quarter mile of a developed area, mostly boat-access. Site limit is 8 persons and one RV unit. Vault toilets at all campgrounds. The NPS page shows an alerts link and no alert text. DARKSKY: no Amistad entry found. A darksky.org news item in search results names Devils River State Natural Area, a Dark Sky Sanctuary near Del Rio; its distance was not checked and it is not in this batch's list.
